invariants: External email effects carry a stable idempotency key across retries (SHA-256 of the rendered request), and the bounded 24-hour provider retention is documented rather than claimed as exactly-once.

The transport choice is profile-driven configuration (spring.autoconfigure exclude + ConditionalOnProperty), not code paths: production selects Resend explicitly, development and tests keep SMTP/GreenMail.
RESEND_API_KEY lives only in the deployment secret store (Railway preserve()); the properties record fails fast at boot when the key is absent while the provider is resend.
Retry, circuit-breaker, concurrency-limit, and observation annotations ride the Resend send path exactly as the SMTP path carried them.
doors: EmailSender.send (the transport-neutral contract) — the notifications path calls the EmailSender INTERFACE directly (EmailNotificationService holds Optional<EmailSender>, never the EmailService SMTP class); the provider configuration selects which implementation binds
EmailServiceAutoConfiguration (SMTP path, provider=smtp or missing) and ResendEmailSenderAutoConfiguration (provider=resend) — mutually exclusive by ConditionalOnProperty
marketplace-app application.yml / application-prod.yml / application-dev.yml / application-test.yml profiles
.railway/railway.ts variable declaration (RESEND_API_KEY preserve) — the deployment-composition door (B6/D10 matrix)

findings.scenario: A production deployment sends transactional email while Railway blocks outbound SMTP on the plan tier, so the SMTP transport times out (SocketTimeoutException to smtp.resend.com:587) and every notification email leg fails
findings.invariant: Production email rides an HTTPS provider API (Resend) with stable idempotency keys and secret-store credentials; SMTP stays the development/test channel; no secret value ever enters Git
findings.note: Railway's documented SMTP block on the plan tier is the provider-side cause (Railway docs; measured SocketTimeoutException in production logs). Fixed in this PR by the Resend HTTPS transport. Status registered: the merge itself is owner-gated — RESEND_API_KEY must exist in the Railway secret store before merge/deploy (the PR's own merge precondition), so the remaining risk is an owner decision, not repository code.
